issue_title: Cairo headers in OS X
issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The Homebrew build steps currently **almost** work for OS X on M1 chips. The only issue is that cairo headers imported in the files listed below refer to `cairo/*.h` instead of the header directly. (That is, they name the header in a directory cairo.)
- src/control/PdfCache.h
- src/pdf/base/XojCairoPdfExport.cpp
- src/pdf/base/XojPdfPage.h
- src/view/PdfView.h

To get the code to compile, I have to remove the directory part of the imported headers.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I think this is just a problem with the pkg-config files for cairo in Linux compared to OS X. When calling `pkg-config cairo --cflags` I get the following include library added `-I/opt/homebrew/Cellar/cairo/1.16.0_5/include/cairo`. I expect that on linux the last directory is not there? This should be fixable using CMake (and removing the directory in the files), maybe just add more include directories by appendix `/cairo` to the ones already added? This would make it work for both Linux and OS X.

issue_title: `@overload` with only one context manager case shows all as context managers
issue_body:
**Describe the bug**

The project is using autodoc with inline Python type annotations.

Given the following function definition (snipped to relevant parts):

```py
@overload
def raises(
    expected_exception: Union[Type[E], Tuple[Type[E], ...]],
    *,
    match: Optional[Union[str, Pattern[str]]] = ...,
) -> "RaisesContext[E]":
    ...


@overload
def raises(
    expected_exception: Union[Type[E], Tuple[Type[E], ...]],
    func: Callable[..., Any],
    *args: Any,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> _pytest._code.ExceptionInfo[E]:
    ...
```

The type `RaisesContext` is a context manager, but `ExceptionInfo` isn't. It is [rendered as follows](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference.html#pytest.raises):

**Expected behavior**

The first case is rendered as `with .. as ..`. The second case is rendered as a regular function.

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest

issue_title: Return indication that Anonymous Authentication is disabled instead of Authentication Error
STRICT DNS cluster without endpoints block CDS
issue_body:
*Title*: *STRICT DNS cluster without endpoints block CDS*

*Description*:
> A STRICT DNS cluster without endpoints as below will always in the warming state which make CDS can not to send new CDS request to control plane. Although it is ok if control plane never restart because control plane will continue to send new cluster config to Envoy. But if control plane restart, Envoy will not send new CDS request to control plane and control plane will not send new cluster config to Envoy. When this problem occurs, all new clusters fail to take effect, causing the route to return 503 + NR. 

```
  clusters:
  - name: service1
    connect_timeout: 0.25s
    type: strict_dns
    lb_policy: round_robin
    load_assignment:
      cluster_name: service1
```

From the source code, I found that if the STRICT DNS cluster does not have endpoints, it will not be able to enter the DNS resolution process, and thus cannot trigger the callback function to complete cluster initialization. This keeps the cluster in a warning state.

Although I know this is a configuration issue, does the community have a plan to address this issue, such as adding additional validations to reject misconfigured configurations, or allowing STRICT DNS clusters with no endpoints to complete initialization directly?

issue_title: Add option to disable committing
issue_body:
# Feature Request

<!-- The version of the action you're using -->
- **SVGO Action version**: v1.2.0

<!-- The context in which the action is running -->
- **On**: _any_<!-- choose from: 'push', 'pull_request' -->

## Description

Add a configurable option to prevent this Action from creating a commit, but instead changing the files "on disk". The idea behind this would be to allow further changes to the repository and create a single commit at the end of a Workflow.

This is different from the [`dry-run`](https://github.com/ericcornelissen/svgo-action/blob/develop/docs/options.md#dry-run) option in two ways. First, the `dry-run` option is intended for debugging purposes or to try out the Action safely. Secondly, `dry-run` should also not change the files "on disk".

Potentially, this (not committing) would become the default behaviour of this Action at some point - but that would not be until v2 of this Action.

This relates to #302 in that it would be nice for subsequent job steps to be able to check the output value of this Action to see if it did anything.

### Example

n/a

## Proposal

Add an option for [the Workflow file configuration](https://github.com/ericcornelissen/svgo-action#in-the-workflow-file) named `commit` that accepts a boolean value (`true` or `false`) and commits based on that value. Also, update the `commit` option for [the configuration file](https://github.com/ericcornelissen/svgo-action#in-githubsvgo-actionyml) to allow it to be a boolean value `true` or `false`. If `false`, no commit should be created. If `true`, a commit should be created with the default configuration. If an object, a commit should be created with the object's configuration (same as existing behaviour).

If committing is enabled, the Action should behave as it does currently.

If committing is disabled, the Action should optimize SVGs and make sure they are written "to disk" so that they persist throughout the job.

## Environment info
     
- `adapter-ransformers` version: 2.0.0
- Platform: Darwin-19.6.0-x86_64-i386-64bit
- Python version: 3.6.8
- PyTorch version (GPU?): 1.7.1 (False)

- Using GPU in script?: No.
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No.

## Details

With the removal of the `adapter_names` argument in v2.0.0, adapter models no longer work effectively in multi-threaded contexts.

In our environment, we host adapter models in a GRPC server and make requests to the server for predictions from individual adapters. 

In v1.1.0, concurrent calls for predictions from different adapters work as expected since the `adapter_names` are propagated through each layer in the model.

In v2.0.0, we need to set the global state for the base model using `set_active_adapters` method or the `active_adapters` property. This forces us to acquire a lock for the duration of the forward pass and thus we end up having to process the requests for different adapters serially, which is undesirable.

Is it possible to add the `adapter_names` argument back to the forward method signature to support multi-threaded use cases for adapters?

issue_title: Move --host ordering fix to v3.0.x, v3.1.x, v4.0.x?
issue_body:
Per #6298, we had an accidental change in behavior of `mpirun --host aaa,bbb` between version v2.1.x and v3.0.x.  A fix just went in to master in #6493.

Here's what happened:

* v2.0.x: behavior X
* v2.1.x: behavior X
* v3.0.x: switch to behavior Y
* v3.1.x: behavior Y
* v4.0.x: behavior Y
* master (to become v5.0.x): after PR #6493, back to behavior X

The question is: should we put this fix on any of v3.0.x, v3.1.x, and/or v4.0.x?

## Summary of behavior change

### Behavior X

The ordering of hosts in the `--host` list matters:

```
$ mpirun --host aaa,bbb rank_test
aaa: MCW rank 0
bbb: MCW rank 1
$ mpirun --host bbb,aaa rank_test
aaa: MCW rank 1
bbb: MCW rank 0
```

### Behavior Y

The ordering of hosts in the `--host` list does not matter (**note:** this behavior was unintentional.  It was always intended that we honor the ordering of hosts in the `--host` list):

```
$ mpirun --host aaa,bbb rank_test
aaa: MCW rank 0
bbb: MCW rank 1
$ mpirun --host bbb,aaa rank_test
aaa: MCW rank 0
bbb: MCW rank 1
```

## Discussion points

We need to discuss this and decide what to do.  Points (in no particular order):

1. This is a fairly minor change in behavior.
1. Apparently no one noticed this change in behavior between v2.1.x and v3.0.x.  It was only discovered recently by @bturrubiates, a Cisco employee (while using Open MPI for other / unrelated testing).
1. The fix is probably not worth putting into v3.0.x or v3.1.x. 
1. But it *might* be worthwhile to put in to v4.0.x...?
1. That being said, even putting it in v4.0.x is at least *sorta* breaking backwards compatibility.  You could squint at this and call it a bug and therefore allow it in.  Or you could say that it was effectively the behavior of all the v3.x/v4.x releases, and they're backwards compatible with each other, so we should maintain that behavior in v4.0.x.

issue_title: Async schema definition support
issue_body:
### Story

It'd be great to support passing a `Promise<GraphQLSchema>` instead of just a `GraphQLSchema` object to `useServer` and friends. This would support fancy use cases like dynamically generated GraphQL schemas for things like federation or the fancy database-to-graphql tooling.

The reason why it'd be necessary to support async schema as an option in this library instead of having it all be done in userland is that the GraphQL subscriptions server needs to synchronously register `on('message')` handlers with the websocket to receive the init messages and other setup stuff, and then `await` the schema inside itself once operations start.

If instead a user asynchronously built a schema on connection, and then got a server set up to handle the connection, there's a brief but very real moment after when the `ws` library (or whatever) has established the websocket connection and is accepting messages but before the message handlers are set up by `graphql-ws` to listen for those messages and respond to them.
 
I think this is a super niche use case, but I'd love to highlight it anyways to see you fine folks would be interested in PRs adding this functionality. Also, I think that you might be able to get something like this working by returning a promise for `ExecutionArgs` with an asynchronously built schema in the `onSubscribe` option, but my reading of the docs suggests this would only work for subscriptions, and not the other operation types, which would be great to get support for as well.


### Acceptance criteria

- A developer should be able to pass a `GraphQLSchema` or a promise for a `GraphQLSchema` into the `schema` property for a `makeServer` or `useServer`.

[extensions.filters.network.client_ssl_auth.v3.ClientSSLAuth](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/extensions/filters/network/client_ssl_auth/v3/client_ssl_auth.proto#extensions-filters-network-client-ssl-auth-v3-clientsslauth) 

Describes an external serivce that will return a list of valid client cert signatures to allow.   However, once a client envoy service contacts the server and retrieves the valid list, the client envoy will cache the valid list if the upstream `auth_api_cluster` service unresponsive.

---

The full config/repro steps is detailed in my test repo here:
[https://github.com/salrashid123/envoy_mtls](https://github.com/salrashid123/envoy_mtls)


to repro, 
1. Run envoy
  `envoy -c server.yaml --base-id 0 -l debug`
2. Attempt to access upstream service
  this should fail
```curl -v -H "host: http.domain.com"     --resolve  http.domain.com:8081:127.0.0.1    --cert certs/client.crt    --key certs/client.key     --cacert certs/tls-ca-chain.pem      https://http.domain.com:8081/get```
3. Run `auth_api_cluster` service (which appens to be envoy returning static cert)
`envoy  -c certsvc.yaml --base-id 1`
4. Attempt to access upstream service.  
   this will succeed
5. Stop `auth_api_cluster` service
6. Attempt to access upstream service. 
  this will succeed.  Expected fail.

---

Maybe this is working as intended but i expected pessimistic authorization.

issue_title: Importing torchvision before DALI hangs pipeline indefinitely
issue_body:
Hi all,

I was recently trying to implement a DALI video reader to increase the speed at which I can provide video data to the GPU for a pytorch task. However, I was getting weird behavior where sometimes one or two batches could be loaded before the entire loading pipeline deadlocks indefinitely (no output). Ctrl+c does not stop the program at this point either, so the only way to stop it is to suspend the program (ctrl+z) and/or issue a `kill -9` to the job.

After much painful debugging, I was able to narrow down the problem (or at least one way it can occur, there may be more!). Basically, `import torchvision` (or _most_ but not _all_ submodules of torchvision, e.g. importing *just* the torchvision MNIST dataloader _does not_ cause the issue) **BEFORE** importing any `import nvidia.dali...` will cause this issue. Importing torchvision **AFTER** dali means the issue does not show up!

Here is a minimal example of a working script: https://gist.github.com/ndalton12/0f1900a411150f1dfb9b1ac6384d9889.

Here is a minimal example of a not working script: https://gist.github.com/ndalton12/b888395646cebe319f78006faa0b6f6a. The script never gets past printing the "doing the thing".

Note the only meaningful difference between these two scripts is that the not working one imports torchvision at the top. However, if you change the not working script to import torchvision after the dali imports instead, it will work as expected.

GDB does not show anything useful, just a bunch of threads starting, then nothing.

Version info:
torchvision-0.9.1-py38_cu111
nvidia-dali-cuda110       1.1.0 
pytorch-lightning         1.3.0rc1
cudatoolkit               11.1.1
pytorch                   1.8.1           py3.8_cuda11.1_cudnn8.0.5_0

Also, the `"/data/critical_view_clips/"` directory looks as such:
```
/data/critical_view_clips:
- class1
  - file1.mp4
  - file2.mp4
  - etc
- class2
  - file1.mp4
  - file2.mp4
  - etc
```
All the files are valid since they work in the working example I provided and I already cleaned the non-valid video files.

issue_title: Invalid Maven POM kills transitivity for all dependecies
issue_body:
I was just taking a quick look at your tool because it does for Spock what a small subset of my own tool [Sarek](https://github.com/SarekTest/Sarek) also does for Spock, JUnit 4/5, TestNG and others, namely making final classes and methods mockable.

When playing with it, I noticed that **I had to redeclare your transitive dependencies SLF4J, Avaje Agent Loader, ByteBuddy in order to avoid "class not found" exceptions.** I found the root cause like this:

```text
mvn -X dependency:tree
(...)
[WARNING] The POM for io.github.joke:spock-mockable:jar:1.0.0 is invalid, transitive dependencies (if any) will not be available: 2 problems were encountered while building the effective model for io.github.joke:spock-mockable:1.0.0
[ERROR] 'dependencies.dependency.version' for net.bytebuddy:byte-buddy:jar is missing. @ 
[ERROR] 'dependencies.dependency.version' for org.spockframework:spock-core:jar is missing. @ 
```

From your POM on Maven Central:

```xml
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>net.bytebuddy</groupId>
      <artifactId>byte-buddy</artifactId>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
    <!-- (...) -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.spockframework</groupId>
      <artifactId>spock-core</artifactId>
      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
```

As you can see, the version numbers for Spock Core and ByteBuddy are indeed missing. But this also kills transitivity for the other dependencies because the POM is regarded as invalid. When I locally edited the POM and added versions like 1.3-groovy-2.5 for Spock and 1.10.13 for ByteBuddy, everything was fine.

issue_title: Improve error handling when making requests
issue_body:
When api.honeybadger.io fails due to an error (rare, but it can happen, as in #47), webpack compilation fails with a cryptic error:

```
ERROR in HoneybadgerSourceMapPlugin: failed to upload app.bundle.js.map to Honeybadger API: Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0
```

This specific error message resulted from nginx returning a generic 500 error page rather than a JSON response (which is what an error in our API should generate).

Let's add some error handling so that any non-successful response from the server is logged with a warning that the source map upload failed so that the webpack build can continue without erroring out.

issue_title: How to perform a relative scaling augmentation?
issue_body:
I'm building a custom segmentation pipeline, meant to work with different datasets of different sizes, as well as producing images of different sizes. On some stage of the data augmentation, I want to make my objects more variable in size, which I want to do by scaling them by a random *factor*. I tried the obvious choice, `dali.ops.Resize`, and found that it expects me to know absolute pixel values for the resulting image. However, I don't know them (can't compute them), because at the time of building the pipeline I don't know the input size. I tried to `dir` an `EdgeReference` but it doesn't seem to contain any of that information.

So, the question is, can I (1) go around that somehow, and maybe combine other operators to achieve a relative scaling without knowing the exact size, or (2) obtain the image shape information within a pipeline's runtime? Or is it something that has to be more or less hard-coded for each dataset?

issue_title: Retrieving socket options in access loggers
issue_body:
Problem we're trying to solve: extract downstream/upstream remote socket options for use in an access logger.

I think we can do this for downstream via a custom listener filter that has access to the Socket and place this in dynamic metadata, which the access logger can then consume.

I don't see a mechanism to do this upstream, upstream network filters don't have a way to reach into the Socket.

1. Is this a correct assessment of the current situation?
2. Would it be reasonable to provide upstream network filters the ability to peek at the Socket for getsockopt (possibly wrapped to limit interactions to only this method)?
3. Is there a more principled way we could ask Envoy to collection a set of socket options and make them available for logging? I can imagine a config option to specify which socket options to collect, alongside which ones to set as we have today.

CC @florincoras @mattklein123 @eziskind

issue_title: Fix operator== of separatrices
issue_body:
it currently identifies separatrices on different IETs. This should not matter in practice but libflatsurf presently relies on this:

The two sides of an `injectedConnections` (the ones that come from collapsed half edges) in a libflatsurf `FlowDecomposition` live in different `DynamicalDecompositions` and so one's `operator-` is not `operator==` of the other.

issue_title: Why does isort sort packages ending with a number oddly?
issue_body:
Given these, sorted alphanumerically:
```
from bob.apples import aardvark
from bob2.apples2 import aardvark
```
isort reorders them like this:
```
from bob2.apples2 import aardvark
from bob.apples import aardvark
```
Is there a config setting that controls this behaviour? I don't understand the behaviour or the intention here.

Python by default sorts them as I would expect:
```
>>> l= ['from bob2.apples2 import aardvark','from bob.apples import aardvark']
>>> l.sort()
>>> l
['from bob.apples import aardvark', 'from bob2.apples2 import aardvark']
```
So this must be intentional? I've experimented with `force_alphabetical_sort_within_sections` and `lexicographical` and `length_sort` but I can only get accidental success which adversely affects other behaviour.

_(Appreciate this is a contrived example, but it mirrors an actual scenario we have in our production code)._

issue_title: Unique symbol property names are mangled
issue_body:
## Search Terms

unique symbol, mangled name

## Problem

unique symbols looks weird in documentation because it get generated like a normal const

## Suggested Solution

use const name instead of generated const in `unique symbol`

```ts
export const NEOVIS_ADVANCED_CONFIG: unique symbol;
export interface Test {
  [NEOVIS_ADVANCED_CONFIG]?: string; // this will look bad in documentation
}
```

issue_title: Aiohttp get receives 403 response on different machines
issue_body:
🐞 **Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is, on the next line. -->
We have noticed inconsistent behavior using aiohttp client's get while accessing a Tesla auth URL. 
https://auth.tesla.com/oauth2/v3/authorize?client_id=ownerapi&code_challenge=NDgwM2RlMGE1NTEwZWI1NWIzM2Q2NzM3YTRkYTBlZWNjYWMyOGUzZGZiNDJkNmZkNWE3ZDkxNmQ1MzI5YTg0OQ&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=https://auth.tesla.com/void/callback&response_type=code&scope=openid+email+offline_access&state=9_MVz16nNle7FSB8-O50bKZId0XNAgTrrIg9agarIiPBV9GnMtsw3uAHeC3jXNjLjs4CSYrqQ5EQBIy-_fmoVQ

Depending on the machine, sometimes the get works and sometimes we receive a 403 but whatever response is consistent for a particular client machine.  This may be related to changes in a web application firewall setup by Tesla but the fact that the same code on multiple machines (including virtual) from the same network have inconsistent results may indicate an underlying aiohttp issue. 

Using requests with the same headers as aiohttp results in success across all client machines. If we inject a mitmproxy in the middle for the aiohttp code, we avoid the 403 entirely. Curl and web browsers with the same headers also can access the url consistently on the same machines.

We understand that 403 is coming from the Tesla server but the same machine can use other mechanisms with the same headers/cookies and avoid the 403. This behavior also arose recently so it is probably something Tesla did.

issue_title: Flexible way of obtaining capabilities for a device
issue_body:
Hey there,

This is related to **[Issue #574](https://github.com/appium/ruby_lib/issues/574)** where the original poster was inquiring about how to find more capabilities from a single known attribute.

In majority of the use cases, when testing out a device you would know basic attributes such as the device id, the operating system, the operating system version. 

**However here is an alternative context:**

What if your devices sat physically connected to a server in a remote location, and you did not have physical access to it? You knew a basic single attribute like device name or device id, but you did not know if someone at the remote server location updated the device operating system from 10.1.1 to 10.1.2? 

_Put another way:_

What if the capabilities creation for devices was more simple and the code was able to decipher additional attributes. For example, in creating the capabilities for the device we only pass in the UDID and then Appium takes that UDID, scans the server's system for connected devices and from those devices finds the match based on the UDID and then sets operating system, operating system version, etc.

Does Appium have this capability or does it require that these capabilities be known before hand? Or is there a way other developers were able to achieve that scenario I stated above?

Thanks in advance

issue_title: Recalculate screen size on window resize
issue_body:
* `zsh-autocomplete` version: 7662f28a3bca1165efeee853e2571d12837e855d
* Zsh version: 5.8
* Framework: omz
* Plugin manager: zinit

<!-- Please use the following template to put together a minimal test case with which I can
reproduce the bug. If I cannot reproduce the bug, then I cannot fix it! -->
```zsh
 # Make sure you always test with the `main` branch.
$ git -C /path/to/zsh-autocomplete switch main

# Update to the latest commit.
$ git -C /path/to/zsh-autocomplete pull

# Create a temp dir and enter it.
$ cd $(mktemp -d)

# Restart Zsh without config files in this dir.
$ ZDOTDIR=$PWD HOME=$PWD exec zsh -f

# Source the plugin.
% source /path/to/zsh-autocomplete/zsh-autocomplete.plugin.zsh

# Test and document the steps that reproduce the problem.
% <insert your steps to reproduce here>
```
.autocomplete.screen-space only runs on precmd.  Therefore _autocomplete__max_lines  is incorrect  when terminal was resized, prompt was moved up down without command running.  In other words  _autocomplete__screen_space is incorrect in these scenarios until precmd.  Because of this, you can get stuck in loop where every letter typed results in listscroll mode.

```
.autocomplete.async.list-choices.complete() {
   # .autocomplete.screen-space
  local -i _autocomplete__max_lines=$(( _autocomplete__max_lines() ))

```

```
_autocomplete__max_lines() {
  local -i lines; zstyle -s ":autocomplete:${curcontext}:" list-lines lines ||
    lines=16
  return $(( max( lines, _autocomplete__screen_space - BUFFERLINES ) ))
}
```

```
.autocomplete.screen-space() {
  emulate -L zsh; setopt $_autocomplete__options

  local -a reply=()
  print -nr $'\e[6n'
  IFS=$'\e[;' read -Asd R
  local -i y=$reply[-2]
  local -i pslines=${#${(%%)PS1}//[^$'\n']}
  _autocomplete__screen_space=$(( LINES - y - pslines - 2 ))
}
```
Fix would be to recalculate _autocomplete__screen_space before each list-choices

issue_title: glass: UX review
issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I spoke to the UX Product Owner this afternoon and received some really helpful feedback on the process. Generally, she loved the installer look and feel.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Few points she brought up that I think we can change for the better:

Installer notes:
1. When the bootstrap process and the node deployment is running, provide a checklist of items (and have them systematically check off when the process completes). This is useful as if the process continues for too long without information, the user might think it is broken and attempt to restart unnecessarily.

Dashboard notes:
1. The health bar appears to be missing information. Orange = warning, but this isn't clear, a label would help. The problem with icons by thesmelves is that they can easily be confused as something to hover over, rather than a source of information. There is enough room on the bar to include a label and an icon.
2. Capacity is good. However, the colours and the labels might need to be updated. The "unassigned" graph is highlighted red. Is it a warning that this space is not used? "Grey" or something more unassuming is a more suitable colour for unassigned space.
3. System information uses "used" and "free" as the language choices next to the graphs depicting capacity, however, capacity uses "unassigned and "assigned". It's important to use consistent language.
4. If we have navigation (like we did in the Ceph dashboard) keep to the left-hand side. If there will only be a few items to research, try using a menu bar at the top of the dashboard.

Layout notes:
- Swap system information with services (so that important information in colour and numbers) are together. This is because the user can gather information immediately from the images/graphs/numbers, whereas tables are together (services, hosts, volumes)  require further overview
- If the user is intended to interact with any of the volumes/hosts/services widgets, it might be worth having individual navigation sections rather than on the singular dashboard pane (for example, if the user goes up to 40, 50, 100 volumes, how is it going to be displayed properly without breaking the page? Or easily consumable?)

issue_title: Changes to the `.pagination` API
issue_body:
#### What problem are you trying to solve?

Improve `.pagination` API (and possibly performance and stability)

#### Describe the feature

I would humbly suggest the following 2 breaking changes:

- Switch order of `allItems` and `currentItems` parameters of `pagination.paginate`, `pagination.filter` and `pagination.shouldContinue`

My reasoning about parameters order is that probably most use cases don't need the `allItems` parameters, with `currentItems` typically being more used. To be confirmed by other users, but if indeed `currentItems` is used more than `allItems` then it should reflect in the order of parameters.

It doesn't change how the Got code works but could save custom `pagination.paginate`, `pagination.filter` and `pagination.shouldContinue` from having an unused and unaesthetic `_` as the second parameter... ;)

- Default value for `stackAllItem` to `false`

As per the default of `allItems`, it implies a waste of CPU and RAM resources when unused. This is especially noticeable when iterating large datasets (and can results in a node.js crash in worst case scenarios)

#### Checklist

- [x] I have read the documentation and made sure this feature doesn't already exist.

issue_title: Table 317 3D background - confusion over CS and C keys
issue_body:
Table 317 — Entries in a 3D background dictionary

3D support in PDF is currently heavily centred around RGB-based colour spaces - see ColorSpace key in "Table 311 — Entries in a 3D stream dictionary" and many places in clause 13.6 and related sub-clauses. Trying to future-proof things for other colour families for some future PDF version is fraught with potential issues and creates confusion now. Of course, the future is also highly unlikely to support Patterns, named colours or other advanced PDF colour spaces!

Lack of clarity for **CS** and **C** keys with confusing statements about a possible future:

The **CS** key is a "name or array" yet the description explicitly constrains values to only **DeviceRGB** (name) by an explicit shall statement: "The only valid value shall be the name **DeviceRGB**." 

It then goes on to state "PDF consumers shall be prepared to encounter other values that may be supported in future versions of PDF.". Clearly, the intention is that the array format might be one of the other PDF colour spaces, but this is no different to handling future PDF features anywhere else in PDF as described in "Annex I (normative) PDF versions and compatibility". So this second explicit "shall" makes no sense with the other explicit "shall" statement. 

- Change **CS** Type to just "name" (delete "or array").
- Delete the confusing "PDF consumers ..." sentence.

Correspondingly the **C** key is typed as "(various)" with a description that doesn't really help, except for the **DeviceRGB** case (which is the only valid current color space as mandated by the **CS** "shall" statement!). It needs to be reworded to a similar statement to the C key from "Table 166 — Entries common to all annotation dictionaries": 

"An array of 3 numbers in the range 0.0 to 1.0, representing the background colour in the colour space defined by the **CS** key". 

If/when 3D ever supports other colour spaces, this would just be one place of many that need careful review and updating.

When creating a new pack (and probably when editing), the version field only accepts numbers, at the least it should accept a `.` too, and probably any characters. Adding a letter to the end gets that stripped off and just the number left.

issue_title: SizeofError for Struct and Sequence
issue_body:
(I'm using construct 2.9.45)

When I try to use sizeof() for a dynamic Struct that requires a context it produces a SizeofError that it cannot find the key. (This also happens for Sequence and FocusedSeq)

```python
from construct import *


spec = Struct(
    'count' / Int32ul,
    'entries' / Byte[this.count]
)

print(spec.sizeof(count=3))
```

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
   ...
construct.core.SizeofError: cannot calculate size, key not found in context
```


It seem that removing lines 2011 and 2012 (https://github.com/construct/construct/blob/master/construct/core.py#L2011) seems to fix the issue, but only if the Struct is at the first level. Doing something like this will still fail:

```python
spec = Struct(
    'a' / Int32ul,
    'b' / Struct(
        'count' / Int32ul,
        'entries' / Byte[this.count]
    )
)

print(spec.sizeof(**{'b': {'count': 3}}))
```

I believe this may be due to it not setting up a context container that is relative to the current Construct being evaluated like it was in 2.8.

### Bug description
JupyterHub with SwamSpawner **IS** spawning a docker container on the remote host, but this docker container when tries to reach to the jupyterhub master container **fails**.


#### Expected behaviour

Start Jupyter notebook on remote host and connect to jupyterhub master to proxy it.

#### Actual behaviour

Start Jupyter notebook on remote host but is not able to connect to jupyterhub master to proxy it.

### How to reproduce

#### Dockerfile:

``` Dockerfile
# base image: jupyterhub
# this is built by docker-compose
# from the root of this repo
FROM jupyterhub/jupyterhub
# install dockerspawner from the current repo
RUN pip install --no-cache dockerspawner
# install dummyauthenticator
RUN pip install --no-cache jupyterhub-dummyauthenticator oauthenticator
# load example configuration
ADD jupyterhub_config.py /srv/jupyterhub/jupyterhub_config.py
ADD userlist /srv/jupyterhub/userlist
```

#### docker-compose.yml

``` yaml
version: "3"
services:
  jupyterhub:
    env_file: .env
    build:
      context: "."
      dockerfile: "Dockerfile"
    image: swarm_jupyterhub:latest
    # This is necessary to prevent the singleton hub from using its service number as its hostname
    hostname: jupyterhub
    # Permit communication with the host's docker server
    volumes:
      - "/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock"
      - "./jupyterhub_config.py:/srv/jupyterhub/jupyterhub_config.py"
      - "./userlist:/srv/jupyterhub/userlist"
    # Ensure Hub and Notebook servers are on the same network
    networks:
      - jupyterhub_network
    environment:
      DOCKER_NETWORK_NAME: jupyterhub_network
    # Ensure that we execute on a Swarm manager
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
      placement:
        constraints:
          - node.role == manager
networks:
  jupyterhub_network:
    driver: overlay
    #external: true
```

TYPE emp_det is RECORD
(

CREATE TYPE employee_pkg.emp_det AS (

);

issue_title: Update allowable field_format values per Standards Reference definition regarding [+|-] characters
issue_body:
Initial issue identified:

> Line 105 of the attached .xml has
>   <field_format>%+8s</field_format>
> even though data_type is ASCII_STRING, and page 29 of the Standards says, "In PDS4 labels, the "+" is forbidden for string fields."
> 
> OK, I apologize that this is so ticky-tack, but the real data file had -, and the data was not left-justified, and validate flagged that to my surprise. So this is your penalty for catching something so minute in the first place.

Conversation between @mcayanan and @rjoyner

> I definitely agree that the constraints listed below should be validated.  Just not sure SCH is the most efficient ?  In the past we have discussed that Validate validate stuff that couldn’t be (easily) validate in SCH ?
> Let’s discuss…
>  
> [+|-]
> Either a "+" or "-", but never both. The "-" may be used for string fields, to indicate that the string is (or should be) left-justified in the field. This is actually the preferred way to present most string values in character tables, so the field_format value for fields with a data type of ASCII_String will nearly always begin with a "-". Similarly for any of the date/time type fields. In PDS4 labels, the "-" prefix is forbidden for all numeric fields (integers, floating point numbers, and numbers using scientific notation).
> The "+" may be used with numeric fields to indicate that an explicit sign is included in the field for input, and should be displayed on output. In PDS4 labels, the "+" is forbidden for string fields.
>  
> (1)    SCH to ensure -- Either a "+" or "-", but never both.
>  
> SCH to ensure the constraints would be enforced in accordance with the  <data_type>. 
>  
> (2)    So, I think all of the following <data_type>  values would NOT allow “+“:
>  
> ASCII_Short_String_Collapsed
> ASCII_Short_String_Preserved
> ASCII_String
> ASCII_Text_Collapsed
> ASCII_Text_Preserved
>  
>  
> (3)    All of the following <data_type> values would NOT allow “-“:
>  
> ASCII_NonNegative_Integer

> ASCII_Numeric_Base2
> ASCII_Numeric_Base8

issue_title: unused npm dev dependencies, once added by Vaadin, are never removed
issue_body:
Vaadin has a list of 'required npm dependencies' that are automatically added into `package.json` during the `prepare-frontend` step (by the Vaadin Maven plugin [during the build](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/blob/bbfa1e7e655e35f5c2d280248899eab3e92ac0e7/flow-maven-plugin/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/plugin/maven/PrepareFrontendMojo.java#L137) or by the Vaadin DevMode handler [during the starup](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/blob/bbfa1e7e655e35f5c2d280248899eab3e92ac0e7/flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/startup/DevModeInitializer.java#L373-L388)). If a dependency is no longer needed in a later Vaadin version, it's removed from the list of 'required dependencies', so it's no longer automatically added to `package.json` by Vaadin. However, if a dependency was required in an earlier Vaadin version and is not needed anymore in a later Vaadin version, it remains in `package.json` making the `npm install` phase of the build / statup slower and potentially leading to version conflicts.

With Vaadin 19.0.0.alpha1 this is the case with the following dependencies:
 - webpack-babel-multi-target-plugin (removed in 65b43f3 / 3.0.0.beta2)
 - progress-webpack-plugin (added in edc43a1 / 3.1.0.alpha1, removed in 244f81c / 5.0.0.alpha1)
 - terser (added in 1b2b3ba / 3.1.0.alpha1, removed in 08862de / 3.2.0.alpha7)
 - raw-loader (removed in 04b1692 / 5.0.0.alpha1)

After manually removing obsolete dependencies the build time of the default start.vaadin.com V19 Fusion project went down by about 10%
 - [when pnpm downloads everything from the Internet] by ~7 seconds: from 50 to 43 sec
 - [when pnpm takes everything from the local cache] by ~2 seconds: from 17 to 15 sec

**Steps to reproduce**:
1. create a new Vaadin 19 / Fusion project with [https://start.vaadin.com/?preset=fusion](https://start.vaadin.com/?preset=fusion)
   (or with Vaadin CLI: `npx @vaadin/cli init --fusion --pre unused-deps-test`)
2. see that `package.json` contains the 4 obsolete dependencies mentioned above (since this is a project that was sequentially updated through every Vaadin version in history)
2. (optional) clean the local pnpm packages store to simulate a clean dev machine: `rm -rf ~/.pnpm-store`

issue_title: parseStringLiteral treats single quote and double quoted strings the same wrt escaping
issue_body:
I'm working through a difference in input handling between this and other liquid libraries, specifically wrt string literals, in this example:

```
{{ value | replace :  '"' '\"' }}
```

These two string literals are interpreted by JS as 
1. `["'", "\"", "'"]` aka single quote, escaped double quote, single quote in a 3 char string
2. `["'", "\\", "\"", "'"]` aka single quote, escaped backslash, escaped quote, single quote in a 4 char string

the two pieces are parsed by `parseStringLiteral` excerpt, my read of this is that we skip the first char being the quote (!) and then treat proceeding escape chars the same whether the string literal uses single or double quotes, to do escaping as expected there should be two paths a single quote path and a double quote path? If started with single quote, then `\"` is two chars, if started with double quote then `\"` is one char (escaped quote).

```
...
for (let i = 1; i < str.length - 1; i++) {
    if (str[i] !== '\\') {
      ret += str[i]
      continue
    }
...
```

This has the impact in my simple example of making the replace filter never fire, as the parseStringLiteral method considers these two strings equivalent.
